I will keep cotton as the main crop this year, same as I usually do, because on 7.5 mu I cannot spread myself too thin. I have farmed 40 years, so I do not start from zero. I start from what worked before and then adjust a little. With well irrigation, I am not as afraid of spring drought, so I can push fertilizer a bit to protect yield. Cotton is still my steadier crop here, so I will put more land into it. Stevia can make money too, but it needs cleaner management and more careful cutting, so I will keep it on a smaller area. I will use improved seed or seedlings for both, because if neighbors get better stand and better yield from improved material, I will follow that. On fertilizer, I will not be stingy at the start of the season. If I underfeed and lose yield, that hurts more than spending a bit extra on one more bag. For cotton I will feed more nitrogen and potash because I want strong growth and boll setting. For stevia I will keep fertility balanced, because too much nitrogen can make it grow too soft. I will use ploughing where I want the land opened up well before planting, then manage water by the well according to weather. On pests, I will spray by the season I usually see in the field, not wait until damage gets serious.
